legend: Spectral karyotype from a patient with myelodysplastic neoplasm who had mutant TP53 (variant allele frequency [VAF]: 63.6%) and concomitant loss of a TP53 allele by cytogenetically visible deletion of 17p in a highly complex karyotype with involvement of chromosomes 1, 4, 5 (5q deletion), 6, 7, 9, 11, 12, 16, and 17.

Bone marrow trephine biopsy from a case with TP53 missense mutation and concomitant loss of the other TP53 allele detected by FISH (<<36244>>). p53 immunohistochemistry demonstrating mutant protein accumulation in a sizeable proportion of myeloid cells (<<36245>>).

Bone marrow trephine biopsy from a case with TP53 missense mutation and concomitant loss of the other TP53 allele detected by FISH (<<36244>>). p53 immunohistochemistry demonstrating mutant protein accumulation in a sizeable proportion of myeloid cells (<<36245>>).

Interphase FISH analysis of bone marrow aspirate from a patient with myelodysplastic neoplasm using a TP53 probe set (red signal: TP53 locus in 17p13; green signal: control locus in 17q11.2 [NF1]). Five interphase nuclei are shown: two normal nuclei (showing two red and two green signals) on the left (middle and bottom cells), and three abnormal nuclei with a TP53 deletion (showing one red and two green signals) on the left (upper cell) and the right (both cells).
